name: Shabana Mahmood
role: UK Home Secretary (2025–present); Labour MP for Birmingham Ladywood since 2010; former Justice Secretary and Lord Chancellor
summary: As Home Secretary, Mahmood introduced tighter settlement rules and advocated controlled immigration and integration. She voted to renew the UK nuclear deterrent and against legalising assisted dying, and she has advocated a two-state settlement for Israel and Palestine.

notes:
Frontbench speeches (2010-15 Treasury and education briefs) and votes as a minister follow party and Government lines, so those answers are held at medium or low. She resigned from Corbyn's shadow Treasury team over economics,; the most recent clear statements are used. Her Spectator interview with Michael Gove and Times interviews were not opened.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 17 answers taken from it, 17 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; previous answers not consulted. Full active list and remaining nulls reviewed. Living person: no inference. Speeches, the full accessible Katy Balls interview, constituent correspondence and personally labelled committee answers were read alongside selected recorded divisions; vote collection was partial, not a complete career voting history. September committee reading covers the opening policing sections, not the full hearing. The 2025 Gove podcast description was accessible but its full interview was not, so its advertised subjects are not scored. Agency proposals, announcements and implemented policy are distinguished. Settlement consultation is not treated as an already enacted universal ten-year requirement. Police AI supports human assessment rather than transferring governmental decisions to algorithms; offender tagging does not itself establish an opinion on counterterrorism surveillance. Child safeguards do not establish a general adult pornography prohibition. Opposition to self-ID alone does not resolve the broader legal protection of transgender people; immutable biological sex is not an assertion that gender is wholly biological. Opposition to extending abortion time limits does not establish opposition to abortion in most cases; the Northern Ireland commissioning vote is too indirect to settle that broad wording here. Faith-guided personal conduct and religious participation do not establish scriptural civil law, divine political authority, church establishment or denominational parties. Palestinian statehood does not establish a distinctly Jewish-state doctrine; condemnation of ethnic cleansing is not silently relabelled a formal genocide recognition. The NHS motion title alone is insufficient to establish the precise universal-healthcare wording, and living-wage incentives are not automatically a substantial statutory minimum-wage increase. Means-tested asylum support does not establish that all social spending should replace universal provision. Border controls do not establish ethnic assimilation or minority expulsion. Ecology and technology searches and selected environment votes yielded no adequately specific position on the ecological statements. None of the ten listed Marxist, revolutionary or class-theory priorities was directly established; faith alone is insufficient to resolve the religion-illusion proposition. No inference is drawn from Labour membership or a social-conservative label.

November 2026 pass searched Hansard, official divisions, committee evidence, government speeches and constituent writing. It checked tax, employment, healthcare and strikes (economy), elections, courts and policing (government and liberty), marriage, religious exemptions, education, citizenship and immigration (society and culture), interventions, treaty commitments and trade (world and globalism), and energy, climate, biometrics and online regulation (ecology and technology). Commons division searches were selective. Wikipedia appears only in historical answer versions.
